title: Customer Approval & Legal Checklist (Case Studies + Reference Program)
author: Sofia Mendes
body:
## Purpose
This checklist defines the required approvals, artifacts, and review steps to publish a customer case study (web + PDF) and/or to confirm a customer is eligible for scheduled reference calls. It is designed to be repeatable, auditable, and safe for regulated customers.

This page covers:
- Quote verification and attribution rules
- Logo usage approval
- Security/compliance language review
- Final sign-off path (Marketing + Legal + customer)
- Required artifacts and where to store them

## Scope
**In scope**
- Public case study assets: web page, PDF download, blog-style post, social snippets, sales deck slide(s)
- Reference program assets: internal reference profile, reference-call boundaries, approved topics list

**Out of scope**
- Press releases and co-marketing announcements (follow Comms/PR workflow)
- Product claims not supported by current SLAs or documented capabilities

## Definitions (quick)
- **Customer-facing asset:** Anything a prospect or the public can access (website, PDF, decks shared externally, marketplace listing copy).
- **Named vs. anonymized:** Named includes customer name and/or logo; anonymized removes identifying details. Note: some customers consider architecture diagrams identifying.
- **Approved claim:** A statement that has (a) an internal validation owner and (b) explicit customer approval if it references the customer’s environment, outcomes, or internal operations.

## Roles & responsibilities
- **Marketing (Program Owner / PMM):** Owns draft narrative, asset production, and approval coordination.
  - Primary: Camila Reyes (program owner), Soojin Lee (messaging)
- **AE / CSM:** Owns relationship, coordinates customer approvers, ensures the customer understands time commitment and boundaries.
  - Primary: AE for account + Rachel Kim (CS) for reference readiness
- **Solutions Engineering (SE):** Validates technical accuracy (architecture + metrics methodology).
  - Primary: Markus Klein / Simran Kaur
- **Security/Compliance reviewer:** Reviews security language, deployment descriptions, and anything that could be interpreted as a security guarantee.
  - Primary: Naomi Feldman
- **Legal:** Owns release form, NDA/MSA constraints, final legal clearance.
  - Primary: Sofia Mendes; escalation to Michael Grant (GC)

## Required artifacts (what must exist before publishing)
Store all artifacts in the customer’s folder under: **Google Drive → Shared drives → Go-to-market → Reference Program → Customer Approvals → [Customer Name]**

**Required for any public case study (named or anonymized)**
1) **Final case study copy** (Google Doc) + **final designed PDF** (if applicable)
2) **Metrics Validation Worksheet** completed and signed off (SE + Marketing)
3) **Customer Quote & Logo Release Form** (executed) OR an email approval that explicitly covers all items (see “What counts as approval”)
4) **Security language review confirmation** (Security reviewer + Legal acknowledgment)
5) **Customer final sign-off** on the exact assets to be published (web URL preview + PDF)

**Required for reference-call-only participation (no public asset)**
1) Reference program participation email confirming: willingness, frequency, topics, and scheduling windows
2) Internal **reference profile** including boundaries (do/don’t), approved topics, and escalation contact
3) If customer name may be shared privately with prospects: confirm via email (“OK to disclose participation on 1:1 basis”) and store in folder

## What counts as approval (acceptable evidence)
Preferred: **Executed release form** using the template.

If a customer will not sign the form, the following email approval can be accepted **only with Legal confirmation**:
- Email from an authorized approver (typically Marketing/Comms, Legal, or Procurement) stating:
  - Approved company name usage (or anonymized requirement)
  - Approved logo usage (where/how long)
  - Approved quotes (exact text) + speaker name/title approval (or anonymized attribution)
  - Approved claims/metrics (explicit list or attachment)
  - Approved publication channels (website, PDF, sales deck, marketplace listing, social)

**Not sufficient**
- Verbal approval only
- “Looks good” without referencing the specific assets/attachments
- Approval from a non-authorized stakeholder when customer requires Comms/Legal sign-off

## Step-by-step approval flow (public case study)
### Phase 0 — Intake + classification (Marketing owner)
1) Confirm case study type:
   - **Type A:** Public named (logo + name)
   - **Type B:** Public anonymized (no name/logo)
   - **Type C:** Reference-call-only
2) Identify customer approvers and required routing (Comms, Legal, Procurement, Security).
3) Identify Redwood internal reviewers and assign owners:
   - Messaging: Soojin Lee
   - Metrics validation: Markus Klein / Simran Kaur + Sana Farid (measurement notes)
   - Security language: Naomi Feldman
   - Legal: Sofia Mendes
4) Create the Drive folder and add:
   - Draft outline
   - Metrics worksheet
   - Approval tracker doc (simple checklist + dates)

**Exit criteria:** Customer approval path is known and documented; internal owners assigned.

### Phase 1 — Quote capture + verification (Writer + AE/CSM + Legal)
1) Capture quotes via recorded interview notes or written customer responses.
2) For each quote, log the following in the draft:
   - Quote text (exact)
   - Speaker name + title + team (or anonymized attribution)
   - Date captured
   - Context (what question it answers)
3) Verification rules:
   - Do not paraphrase in quotation marks.
   - If the quote mentions numbers (“50% lower cost”), those numbers must match the validated metrics.
   - Titles must reflect the customer’s preferred formatting (e.g., “VP Platform Engineering” vs “Head of Platform”).
4) Send the quote list to the customer for approval as a discrete step if their process is strict.

**Exit criteria:** Quote list is approved or ready for inclusion in the release form.

### Phase 2 — Metrics and claims validation (SE + Marketing + Legal)
1) Complete the **Metrics Validation Worksheet** with:
   - Metric definition (e.g., p95 end-to-end latency, server-side latency, tokens/sec)
   - Measurement window and workload shape
   - Baseline source + Redwood source
   - Caveats/constraints (region, model, sequence lengths, caching enabled)
   - Validation owner + date
2) Acceptable phrasing requirements:
   - Use **“in their production workload”** only if confirmed by the customer and measurement notes.
   - Avoid absolute statements (“eliminated downtime”, “guaranteed compliance”).
   - Tie outcomes to conditions (“with Dedicated capacity and configured fallback policies…”).
3) Legal review focuses on:
   - No implied warranty or universal performance guarantee
   - No third-party trademark misuse
   - No disclosure of confidential information (security controls, incident details, unique architecture identifiers)

**Exit criteria:** Claims list is locked; metrics are validated; approved phrasing is incorporated into the draft.

### Phase 3 — Security language review (Security + Legal)
1) Review any mention of:
   - VPC / on-prem / private networking
   - KMS/HSM, key ownership, encryption
   - Audit logs, retention, data residency
   - Incident response and SLAs
2) Required language patterns:
   - Prefer **capability-based** statements: “Supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations”
   - Avoid **certification inference**: If a customer says “SOC 2-ready,” ensure we do not claim the customer’s compliance.
   - Avoid describing control implementation details beyond what Redwood already documents publicly.
3) For regulated customers, redact:
   - Exact regions, IP ranges, vendor names used internally (unless already public)
   - Detailed retention periods if considered sensitive
   - Any security review transcripts or evidence specifics

**Exit criteria:** Security reviewer confirms the asset does not introduce new security commitments or sensitive disclosures.

### Phase 4 — Logo usage confirmation (Marketing + Customer + Legal)
1) Confirm logo usage scope:
   - Where: website, PDF, sales deck, marketplace listing
   - Duration: default 24 months (unless customer requires shorter)
   - Format: full-color, monochrome, clearspace requirements
2) Confirm whether customer requires trademark notice or specific brand guidelines.
3) Confirm whether the customer allows:
   - Homepage “Customers” strip inclusion
   - Partner co-marketing (if applicable)

**Exit criteria:** Logo usage is approved in the release form or explicit email.

### Phase 5 — Final customer sign-off (Marketing owner + AE/CSM)
1) Provide the customer:
   - Web preview link (staging URL)
   - Final PDF
   - Any derivative copy: 1–2 social posts, a 1-slide summary, or marketplace snippet (if planned)
2) Request approval explicitly covering:
   - Quotes (final)
   - Metrics/claims (final)
   - Name/logo usage (final)
   - Publication channels
3) Capture approval evidence and save to Drive.

**Exit criteria:** Customer signs the form or sends explicit approval email referencing the final assets.

### Phase 6 — Redwood final sign-off + publish (Marketing + Legal)
1) Confirm the following are complete:
   - Release form executed (or approved email + Legal OK)
   - Security language review complete
   - Metrics worksheet complete
   - Final asset versions locked (no further edits)
2) Legal final check: ensure release includes the same named entity and approved scope.
3) Publish to web + attach PDF.
4) Post-publish:
   - Send customer the live link(s)
   - Save the final published HTML/PDF snapshot to Drive

**Exit criteria:** Asset is live; artifacts stored; internal reference profile updated.

## Final sign-off path (who must approve what)
**Default internal sequence**
1) Marketing (Soojin Lee) → 2) SE validation (Markus Klein / Simran Kaur) → 3) Security reviewer (Naomi Feldman, if security language present) → 4) Legal (Sofia Mendes) → 5) Customer approver(s) → 6) Marketing publish

**Escalate to GC (Michael Grant) if any of the following apply**
- Customer requires non-standard indemnity / liability language in release
- Customer requires removal of Redwood standard withdrawal clause without alternative protections
- Customer asks for performance guarantees, uptime guarantees beyond Redwood SLA, or compliance guarantees
- Customer is a regulated entity and requires detailed security architecture disclosure
- Any request to publish incident details, breach references, or explicit vulnerability discussions

## Withdrawal / takedown expectations (standard)
- Redwood will honor a customer request to remove the case study within the timeframe agreed in the release (standard: commercially reasonable, typically within 10 business days).
- Redwood may retain internal copies for recordkeeping.
- If the asset was syndicated (marketplace, partner blog), Redwood will coordinate removal but cannot guarantee third-party cache timing.

## Checklist (copy/paste into the customer folder)
**Pre-draft**
- [ ] Customer case study type confirmed (A/B/C)
- [ ] Customer approvers identified (names + emails)
- [ ] Internal owners assigned (Marketing/SE/Security/Legal)
- [ ] Drive folder created and linked

**Quotes**
- [ ] Quotes captured with speaker attribution
- [ ] Quotes verified (no paraphrase in quotes)
- [ ] Customer approved quote text + attribution

**Metrics/claims**
- [ ] Metrics Validation Worksheet completed
- [ ] Measurement notes include window + workload caveats
- [ ] All quantitative claims appear in worksheet

**Security/compliance language**
- [ ] Security reviewer completed review (if applicable)
- [ ] No new security commitments introduced

**Logo/name usage**
- [ ] Customer approved logo usage scope
- [ ] Brand guidelines received (if required)

**Legal**
- [ ] Release form executed OR explicit approval email accepted by Legal
- [ ] Any NDA/MSA conflicts checked

**Publish**
- [ ] Customer signed off on final web preview + PDF
- [ ] Final assets archived in Drive
- [ ] Reference profile updated (boundaries + approved topics)

## SLA guidance (internal)
- Standard legal review SLA: **3–5 business days** once the draft is final and the release form request is complete.
- Security language review SLA: **2–3 business days**.
- Customer approval timing varies; set expectation of **7–14 days** depending on their internal routing.

## Common pitfalls (avoid)
- Publishing a metric without stating the measurement context (model, region, caching/batching, window)
- Treating an engineering champion’s “OK” as final when customer requires Comms/Legal approval
- Including architecture details that reveal sensitive deployment patterns (especially for Private/VPC)
- Using trademarked competitor names in comparisons without Legal review
